data.plain_english: A new report says China's long housing slump is straining the budgets of its local governments. The council expects Hong Kong shares, especially property companies, banks and tech firms, to keep struggling, and property companies in all four markets to stay under pressure, partly because borrowing costs are rising worldwide. Mainland Chinese banks and energy firms look more stable for now, because their share prices have not shown signs of stress. The council is most divided on American technology companies, which have been rising even as borrowing costs climb. This is research to help you think, not advice to buy or sell anything.
